thread:
lee: quick idea — propose a lightweight prefetch-ownership handoff that avoids a central sequencer. ownership token = (epoch, owner_id, seq). when a prefix is demoted we forward the token to the new owner and let them continue serving cached kvs while honoring epoch checks. aims: reduce eviction thrash and multiple rehydrates during rapid hotkey oscillation.

maya: curious — how do you avoid split-brain where two nodes think they own the same prefix and both serve writes?

samir: we can make transfer idempotent: the token includes an epoch monotonically increasing on every handoff. receivers accept only tokens with epoch >= current. writers always check token epoch before relying on cached reads.

lee: sketch of token and fast-check pseudo: 
```
struct HandoffToken {
  u64 epoch;
  node_id owner;
  u64 seq; // local monotonic counter to order transfers
  signature sig; // optional HMAC from allocator for safety
}

on_receive(token) {
  if token.epoch < local_epoch_for_prefix { reject(); }
  local_owner = token.owner;
}
```

tess: hmm — what about in-flight mutation ordering? if owner A forwards token to B but A still has in-flight writes, B might serve stale read-after-write.

maya: right. need a small grace-window: either block new reads on B until A ack drain, or accept reads but treat writes as pending until seq ack. both have latency/cost tradeoffs.

samir: alternative: optimistic handoff + short lease overlap. new owner B can serve reads immediately but conservatively validate any write-affecting ops by checking a compacted write-commit watermark from A. watermark can be piggybacked on handoff token.

lee: exact tradeoffs: 
- block reads until drain: strong correctness, higher tail latency during handoff.
- optimistic overlap + watermark: lower latency, need validation path and slightly more metadata.

tess: what about eviction behaviour? does this increase residency if tokens keep getting forwarded quickly? could actually worsen churn.

lee: agree. plan includes eviction backpressure: when a prefix has had N handoffs in T seconds, set it to cooperative mode (more aggressive prefix cold-down) or throttle prefetch. also track hothand count metric.

bench-bot: perf note: local sim shows handoff median cost ~850us, full drain-blocking ~6-10ms under 95th. link: https://bench.redwood/hand_off/17485

maya: rollout + test plan: unit tests for token idempotency, integration sim with chaos (partition + reorder), canary in staging (single zone), prod canary 5% traffic with feature-flag + diagnostics (hothand counter + drain-latency).

samir: fallback: if handoff fails or owner disappears, allocator issues a forced epoch bump with tombstone marker and new token from allocator to avoid dual owners. tombstone ensures any late commits are rejected.

lee: ACK — i'll write a short RFC doc with the token format, state diagram, and rollout checklist. will include metrics: handoff-rate, handoff-failures, handoff-duration-p50/p95, hothand-count, eviction-churn-by-prefix.

maya: sgtm. please add retro hooks to disable if eviction-churn goes up post-rollout. :thumbsup:

tess: small nit — please make token sig optional (config) so private deployments with strict KMS can enable it, others can skip.

lee: good call. will include flag. thanks all.
